# Alexander Campos — campos.works

I work in operations, build software, and write about the systems people depend on. My research interests include compute economics, ownership, and individual agency. My background includes six years in regulated finance. Sovereignty here means the ability to understand and change the systems you depend on, and to retain meaningful choices as circumstances change.

This personal portfolio contains projects, writing, working research, and a resume.

## Selected projects

ForgeFrame: Open-source agent memory over MCP, using SQLite and FTS5. Supports retrieval, use-based strengthening, decay, and protected principles. Project notes: https://campos.works/projects/forgeframe

CREATURE: A personal agent system running on one machine: memory, model routing, scheduled jobs, and approval queues. An experiment in making context, permissions, and failures inspectable. Names such as “dreams” describe scheduled maintenance or model-generated associations; they are not evidence of consciousness or independent intent. Project: https://campos.works/projects/creature. The component inventory at https://campos.works/creature is a frozen snapshot from August 10, 2026, with self-reported operating labels and known limitations.

Reframed: A live resume tool with several analytical perspectives and signed records of text changes. Its receipts document editing; they do not prove a claim is true. Live at https://reframed.works

Distillery: A phone-to-laptop reading workflow. Shared links are analyzed by a local model against recorded interests and principles; selected material is added to memory. Project notes: https://campos.works/projects/distillery

Orellana Tools: A quoting and accounting prototype for a landscaping business in Virginia, with demo workflows, a QuickBooks adapter, and confirmation before accounting writes. Spanish aliases support service entry; generated proposals are English. Production usage is unverified. Case study: https://campos.works/work#orellana

DEUCE: A tennis forecasting experiment that signs forecasts before outcomes are known so calibration can be evaluated. Paper only; no capital at risk. The ledger keeps misses available for review alongside correct forecasts. Project notes: https://campos.works/projects/deuce

## Writing and background

Research: https://campos.works/research/claims-capacity-collateral — “Claims, capacity, and collateral” follows the conversion from financial commitments to working compute, useful output, and cash. It is an exploratory working argument, not a validated investment finding. The longer private draft uses AI research and editing assistance; original project-level measurements are still being developed.

Writing: https://campos.works/writing

“On Observation and Identity Modeling” examines how systems model their users and how those models can affect the people using them. The second part, “Where the Difference Is Stored,” continues that inquiry through research and personal experiments. These essays explore questions about agency and observation; the project descriptions document what the implementations do.

Glossary: https://campos.works/misc (https://campos.works/glossary redirects here). Short definitions support the projects and essays, including terms from neuroscience, machine-learning interpretability, and philosophy of mind.

Work: https://campos.works/work
Resume: https://campos.works/resume
Project archive: https://campos.works/misc/hall-of-shame

## Technical experience

Languages: TypeScript, Python, SQL
Frameworks: Astro, React, Next.js, Electron, Node.js, Flask
AI tooling: Anthropic API, OpenAI API, Ollama, Model Context Protocol, structured tool use, model routing, evaluation and rubric design
Data: SQLite/FTS5, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Splunk
Architecture: Local-first tools, MCP servers, permission boundaries, source provenance, and audit records
Operations: Monitoring, controls, vendor integrations, escalation, and process automation

## Working principles

Make context handling and permissions inspectable; describe each enforced boundary precisely rather than claiming system-wide guarantees.
Preserve the source of retrieved information and distinguish it from model interpretation.
Make consequential actions reviewable before execution.
Evaluate an experiment against recorded outcomes; keep unsuccessful results in the record.
State what a tool can verify and where the implementation is incomplete.
